provenance.prompt_summary: Generate a SOFL requirement model (CDFD + fModule + MES) for the vehicle-level ADAS onboard system from NL-RQ-ADAS-v1, with one Level-1 refinement of the F3 AEB branch; single pass, no self-review.

elements.name: Perception_Localisation
elements.responsibility: Convert E1 raw sensor data and E2 gnss/imu into a fused object table with lead-object identification and into the ego state; write D2 and D3.
preconditions: raw_sensor_data <> null and gnss_imu <> null and map_data <> null and HD_Map_DB <> null

postconditions.effect: ego_pose <> null and object_table <> null and ego_state <> null
HD_Map_DB <> null and Object_Track_DB <> null and Ego_State_DB <> null

invariants: ego_state.yaw_rate <= 3.5 and ego_state.yaw_rate >= -3.5 (A-4 sanity envelope on the localisation output)
elements.notes: D1 is written here because the spec store table lists F5/F1 as owner and D1 is refreshed by E5; F5 is forbidden to write stores, so F1 carries the refresh (see OI-6).

elements.name: Prediction
elements.responsibility: Predict the future motion of the relevant objects over a horizon of at least 3 s and derive the minimum TTC to the ego vehicle.
preconditions: ego_pose <> null and object_table <> null and HD_Map_DB <> null
elements.notes: Section 5 makes F2 the only TTC-computing function, but section 6 has F3.1 compute a TTC set as well; both are modelled (see OI-7).

elements.name: Behaviour_Planning
elements.responsibility: Decide the target manoeuvre (type, target speed, target lane, required deceleration), respect traffic rules and driver intent, and decide whether to issue the driver warning.
preconditions: ego_state <> null and predicted_trajectories <> null and driver_intent <> null and route <> null and HD_Map_DB <> null and Traffic_Rules_DB <> null
elements.notes: Level-0 summary of the AEB branch; the branch is refined in the child module AEB_Branch (F3.1/F3.2/F3.3).

elements.name: Route_Planning
elements.responsibility: Compute the route to the E4 destination: path length, estimated time of arrival and the lane geometry needed by F3 and F5.
preconditions: destination <> null and ego_pose_for_route <> null and HD_Map_DB <> null
elements.notes: No numeric threshold in section 7/8 applies to the route output, so only qualitative postconditions are given (R-G-1).

elements.name: Motion_Planning
elements.responsibility: Convert the manoeuvre into a kinematically feasible trajectory, never exceed the applicable speed limit, and honour the deceleration requirement carried by the manoeuvre.
preconditions: manoeuvre <> null and route_for_motion <> null and ego_state_for_motion <> null and predicted_trajectories_for_motion <> null and traffic_rules <> null and HD_Map_DB <> null and Traffic_Rules_DB <> null
elements.notes: Writes D4 because the spec store table names F5 as owner of D4 and states D4 is refreshed by E6, while section 5 forbids F5 to write stores (see OI-6).

elements.name: Control
elements.responsibility: Convert the trajectory into an actuation command (longitudinal acceleration, brake, steering) kept inside the actuator envelope.
elements.notes: Produces E9 actuator_cmd, which is routed to F7 only; it never reaches the actuators directly (R-E-2).

elements.name: Safety_Shield
elements.responsibility: Supervise the actuation command, output a command satisfying the safety envelope even when F6 violates it, preserve the steering command unless it violates the envelope, and enforce the traffic rules.
preconditions: actuator_cmd <> null and Ego_State_DB <> null and Traffic_Rules_DB <> null
elements.notes: Sole producer of E8; the traffic-rule guard uses the ego speed from D3 against the posted limit from D4.

traceability.note: Seven onboard functions; no driving-mode or takeover element is added (see OI-1).
Sensors, GNSS/IMU, HMI, actuators, navigation, cloud and V2X appear only as E1-E9 endpoints with belongToType=outSide.
No detector, tracker, planner or controller internals are modelled; F3 is refined only into the branch required by section 6.
Level 1 refines exactly one Level-0 function (F3) into three sub-functions.
These are the only output flows crossing the boundary.

traceability.realised_by: active flow actuator_cmd and the Safety_Shield postconditions
traceability.note: E9 is modelled as the internal F6 -> F7 flow (see OI-5); F7 is the only producer of E8.
D1 and D4 are written by their owner function only (see OI-6 for the F5 contradiction).
Reads are exactly the list of section 5.1: D1 -> F1,F2,F3,F4,F5; D4 -> F3,F5,F7; D3 -> F6,F7.
Exactly 7 processes, 4 data stores, 9 external interfaces; no extra element.

Every process carries a precondition, a postcondition and at least one quantified constraint where section 7/8 gives a threshold; F4 has only qualitative postconditions because no threshold applies to the route.
Matrix covers R-*, F*, N-* and A-* clauses of the specification.
Derived fields and every modelling convenience are declared in README.md and in open_issues.
Each flow is named, directed and has a single producer and a single consumer.
Every produced datum has a named consumer; no output is left without a consumer.
Every datum read in a postcondition is guarded by an explicit <> null precondition.
Object table, lead-object identification and ego state; writes D2 and D3.
Prediction horizon >= 3.0 s (A-7) and minimum TTC reported in the predicted trajectories.
Manoeuvre type/speed/deceleration and the E7 warning; traffic rules and driver intent honoured.
Path length, ETA and lane geometry of the route to E4.
Trajectory with maximum speed, maximum acceleration, deceleration capability, horizon and lateral acceleration.
Actuation command inside the actuator envelope A-3 / A-6.
Shield output satisfying the envelope even for a violating input; steering preserved unless out of envelope; D4 enforced.
AEB branch guaranteed for ego_state.speed <= 130.0 km/h (realised in child module AEB_Branch).
Warning raised at TTC <= 3.0 s and in particular at TTC <= 2.0 s, i.e. no later than the 2.0 s cut-out staging point; T_fcw = 1.5 s (A-5).
Emergency deceleration sized from N-3/N-4 as A-1 = 6.0 m/s^2; the > 30 km/h impact-speed reduction is the sizing yardstick, not a runtime threshold.

The CCRb -4 m/s^2 target deceleration is realised as the RSS braking capability 4.0 m/s^2; the 60-130 km/h VUT window and the 20 km/h target speed are assessment-scenario parameters with no runtime element (see OI-14).
Partial: the RSS parameter set (A-2) is applied, but the spec does not restate the d_min closed form (see OI-9).
a_max,accel and a_min,brake from A-2; the response time rho = 0.1 s cannot be expressed (no timing construct, see OI-13).

traceability.realised_by: trajectory.lateral_accel and the A-6 steering envelope
traceability.note: Partial: no numeric lateral-acceleration capability exists in section 7/8 (see OI-10).
Emergency deceleration of 6.0 m/s^2; realised in full in the Level-1 Maneuver_Planning.
a_max,accel = 2.0 and a_min,brake = a_max,brake = 4.0; rho = 0.1 s not formalised (see OI-13).
Longitudinal actuation envelope 3.0 m/s^2 in F6 and F7.
Yaw-rate sanity envelope on the localisation output.
T_risk_high = 3.0 s and T_fcw = 1.5 s; realised in the child module AEB_Branch.
Normalised steering envelope +/- 1.0, with steering preservation inside the envelope.
Prediction horizon 3.0 s.

open_issues.issue: The seven-function split of section 5 is sufficient for the stated ODD only if driver monitoring stays an external input: no separate driver-monitoring function is added because R-L0-1 forbids extra elements, but a full SAE L2 handover would need one.

D3 ownership is accepted as specified (written by F1, read by F6/F7) because section 5.1 assigns those reads explicitly and R-L0-1 forbids a dedicated ego-state function, so F1's update rate becomes a safety dependency of the shield.

A timing requirement is needed for the emergency branch to be meaningful: the spec fixes thresholds but no cycle time, and SOFL has no timing construct, so rho = 0.1 s (A-2) and the derived 1.39 s braking duration are not formalised.

The AEB branch of F3 is a defensible Level-1 refinement, but refining the F6/F7 actuation chain would cover N-7 and R-E-2 better, because the numeric lateral-acceleration capability and the response time are both missing there.

E9 is listed in section 3 among the external interfaces, but sections 5 and 5.1 place it inside the system as the F6 -> F7 command, so it is modelled as an internal active flow and not as a boundary flow.

Section 4 names F5/F1 as owner of D1 and F5 as owner of D4, while section 5 forbids F5 to write any store and section 5.1 lists only F1 -> D2/D3 as writes, so the model has F1 write D1 (from E5) and F5 write D4 (from E6) to keep E5 and E6 consumed and to satisfy R-D-1.

Section 5 makes F2 the only TTC-computing function while section 6 has F3.1 compute a TTC set, so TTC is computed twice in the model and the responsibility split between F2 and F3.1 is left unresolved.

Section 6 requires a non-zero deceleration manoeuvre for caution but also gives a driver acceleration request precedence for every non-critical risk level, so the caution case with an acceleration request has no consistent rule and the explicit caution rule is modelled.

N-5 does not restate the RSS minimum-safe-distance formula and fixes no unit convention, so the safe-distance requirement is modelled qualitatively through trajectory.min_gap plus the A-2 braking capability instead of as a numeric distance bound.

N-7 has no numeric lateral-acceleration capability in section 7/8 and no steering-to-lateral-acceleration mapping, so trajectory.lateral_accel is carried but cannot be checked numerically by F6 or F7.
Section 8 refers to 'R-F2-1' as the source of the 3.0 s prediction horizon, but no such clause exists in section 5, so the traceability anchor for F2 is missing in the specification.

Derived convenience fields were introduced to carry concepts the spec names but does not enumerate: PredictedTrajectories.lead_gap and lead_speed, Trajectory.min_gap and Trajectory.lateral_accel, and the ego-state flows F1 -> F3 and F1 -> F5 that section 5.1 omits while R-D-2 forbids F3/F5 from reading D3.
The RSS response time rho = 0.1 s cannot be expressed because the SOFL expression grammar and the CDFD have no timing construct, so N-6 is realised only through its acceleration bounds.

The N-4 assessment parameters (VUT 60-130 km/h, target 20 km/h) describe the test scenario rather than a runtime constraint, so they have no model element; the N-4 sizing itself is carried by A-1 and A-2.

Enumerated values (risk level, warning type, manoeuvre type, traffic-signal state, driver-attention state) are encoded as nat codes because the permitted expression grammar contains no string literals; the code tables are listed in README.md.
